### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. palmoplantar keratoderma-sclerodactyly syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.741)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:18398)

**Proposed mechanism:** SMARCAD1 (HGNC:18398) —DISRUPTS→ Loss of function of SMARCAD1; Loss of function of SMARCAD1 —DECREASES→ Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006334); Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006334) —DECREASES→ Epithelial differentiation (GO:0030154); Epithelial differentiation (GO:0030154) —DECREASES→ Abnormal skin development (HP:0000951); Abnormal skin development (HP:0000951) —LEADS_TO→ Adermatoglyphia (HP:0031130); Abnormal skin development (HP:0000951) —LEADS_TO→ Palmoplantar keratoderma with sclerodactyly (HP:0011316). Loss-of-function mutations in SMARCAD1 impair chromatin remodeling, which in turn disrupts epithelial differentiation and subsequently affects skin development, leading to the distinct phenotypes of adermatoglyphia and palmoplantar keratoderma-sclerodactyly syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of a pathogenic gain-of-function variant in SMARCAD1 associated with either disease would refute this hypothesis. Furthermore, observing distinct molecular pathways downstream of SMARCAD1 in each disease, not converging on epithelial differentiation, would also falsify this link.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of SMARCAD1 in skin development opens avenues for therapeutic strategies targeting epithelial differentiation pathways for both adermatoglyphia and palmoplantar keratoderma-sclerodactyly syndrome.

#### 2. absence of fingerprints-congenital milia syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.732)

**Proposed mechanism:** SMARCAD1 (HGNC:10729) —DISRUPTS→ Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006338); Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006338) —LEADS_TO→ Adermatoglyphia (HP:0030189); Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006338) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital milia (HP:0011191); Chromatin remodeling (GO:0006338) —LEADS_TO→ Absence of fingerprints (HP:0011190). **Why it matters:** Understanding the role of SMARCAD1 in chromatin remodeling and skin development could reveal therapeutic targets for regenerative medicine approaches to skin disorders.
